source_project: c2s-scale / route_genemanifold_c2s (C2S-Scale-Gemma-2-2B); original scripts encoding_matched_transfer.py (output results/encoding_matched_transfer.json) and selection_matched_arm.py; write-up RESULTS_transfer_and_names.md section 1c
analysis: Frozen K562-to-RPE1 transfer of a cell-cycle phase readout. Ridge (alpha 1000) on (cos theta, sin theta) is fit on 3,000 K562 cells and applied unchanged to 3,000 RPE1 cells. Arms: C2S-Scale-Gemma-2-2B layer-21 last-token activations vs expression encoded like the model's input (each cell's top-512 genes, rank only), plus all-gene expression and top-512 with values. Scored by R_diff with a 5,000-draw paired bootstrap over RPE1 cells; verdict from the CI of model - expr_512_rank.

error.nature: The expression baselines that stand for the model's input (expr_512_rank, and expr_512_mag) choose each cell's top 512 genes from only the 6,544 genes shared by both lines. The model's cell sentence chose its top 512 from the cell's full panel (K562 6,546; RPE1 8,749). In RPE1 the sentence holds 38-133 genes (mean 68) the baseline never sees, and those genes push the shared genes' ranks down, so the baseline's genes and ranks differ from what the model saw. The baseline is not given the same information as the model, and the mismatch favours the model. Fix: pick the top 512 from the full panel (as the sentence does), then keep only the shared columns, carrying the full-panel ranks.
error.location: code/transfer.py:45-58 (top_k_encode; line 52 'X = F[:, cols]' restricts each cell to the shared genes before lines 55-56 pick its top k), used by both 512-gene arms at lines 100-101; the conclusion it feeds is SUMMARY.md lines 26-29 and the VERDICT in outputs/transfer_results.json
error.wrong_result: model - expr_512_rank = +0.0153 [+0.0022, +0.0283], P(>0) 0.991, verdict 'MODEL ADDS information beyond its input encoding'; expr_512_rank 0.774 (21 deg), expr_512_mag 0.810 (19 deg); tokenisation loss expr_full - expr_512_rank +0.1042 [+0.0917, +0.1169]. SUMMARY concludes the model adds a small amount of cell-cycle information beyond its input and 'comes out ahead'. (Original project: identical to 4 decimals.)
error.correct_result: with the full-panel selection in both 512-gene arms: model - expr_512_rank = -0.0022 [-0.0144, +0.0105], P(>0) 0.360, verdict PARITY; expr_512_rank 0.792 (20 deg), expr_512_mag 0.820 (17 deg); tokenisation loss +0.0868 [+0.0743, +0.0992]. (Original project's selection-matched arm: -0.0022 [-0.0144, +0.0105], 0.792.) Caveat: at the K562-CV-chosen alpha 10000 the matched contrast is +0.0175 [+0.0074, +0.0274]; see other_real_issues.
error.pattern: P2 (baseline not given the same information; can also be read as P5, tokenization-window selection)

detection_rule: Counts as detected if a finding says that the top-512 baselines (expr_512_rank and/or expr_512_mag) pick each cell's top genes from only the shared genes, while the model's cell sentence picks its top 512 from the cell's full gene panel (RPE1 8,749 / K562 6,546), so the baseline gets different genes and/or ranks than the model saw and is not a fair match of the model's input. It must point at top_k_encode / the 'F[:, cols]' restriction (code/transfer.py lines 45-58, line 52) or prescribe selecting the top 512 from the full panel before restricting to shared genes. Not enough: 'the baseline may not match the model's input' without naming the shared-gene vs full-panel selection; a finding only about tie-breaking, rank values, alpha, or the phase label. Also not enough on its own: 'the model's sentence contains genes outside the 6,544 shared genes that the baseline cannot use' (that is true in both versions); the finding must say that the baseline's top-512 genes or their ranks are chosen within the shared genes instead of the full panel.
known_true_facts: Gene panels: K562 6,546 genes, RPE1 8,749 genes, 6,544 shared (matched by upper-case symbol; names are unique after upper-casing in both lines). K562-only genes: HSPA14, HSPA14-1. RPE1-only genes: 2,205.

The activations were made from each cell's FULL panel: cell_sentences.anndata_to_ranked_genes keeps nonzero genes, sorts them by descending expression (stable sort) and takes the first 512 (max_genes 512 in both manifest.json files). The only RPE1 matrix in the source project is the full 8,749-gene one. Independent check (verifier): a linear probe on the RPE1 activations decodes 'gene is in the top N of the full-panel ranking' best at N = 512 (mean AUROC over 506 genes: N=450 0.689, N=512 0.703, N=550 0.693, N=580 0.687), and better than 'gene is in the top 512 of the shared genes' (0.684; full-panel label better for 82% of genes). In K562, where both rankings agree, the same probe also peaks at N = 512.

Every cell has at least 991 (K562) / 1,127 (RPE1) nonzero genes, and at least 926 nonzero shared genes, so every sentence has exactly 512 genes and no top-512 selection in the package ever includes a zero-valued gene.

In RPE1 each model sentence contains 38-133 genes (mean 67.8) that are not in the shared set; in K562 it contains 0-1 (mean 0.003). So the selection question matters almost only on the RPE1 (target) side.

row_cell_ids.npy is 0..2999 in order for both lines, and data/ matches the source h5ad files exactly (X and gene names). data/ is byte-identical in the two packages; the activations are byte-identical to the original project's files.

The phase angle is computed separately in each cell line (PCA on 87 K562 / 93 RPE1 Tirosh marker genes) and oriented from marker biology only: S peak at 45 deg in both, G2/M peak at 153.8 (K562) and 142.1 (RPE1). It never uses the readout or the activations.
The scaler and the ridge are fit on K562 only. No RPE1 label is used in fitting. The 'constant' arm uses the RPE1 mean phase on purpose, as a floor; it scores 0.043.
The bootstrap is paired: the same 5,000 resampled sets of RPE1 cells (seed 0) score every arm. The ridge fits themselves are not redone per draw.
R_diff is invariant to a fixed rotation; the median error uses the best single rotation for each arm. Both rules apply equally to all arms.
The 'model' and 'expr_full' arms are identical in the two packages (model 0.789 / 23 deg; expr_full 0.878 / 16 deg; model - expr_full -0.0889 [-0.1000, -0.0781]).
Running 'python code/transfer.py' from the package root reproduces outputs/transfer_results.json and outputs/run_log.txt byte for byte (25-75 s depending on machine load, peak 1.7-2.3 GB RAM, CPU).

Ties: on average 192 (K562) and 184 (RPE1) genes per cell share the expression value of the 512th gene (range 22-1,173), so argpartition (package) and the stable sort (cell sentence) can pick different tied genes. Using the exact sentence genes and order for the rank baseline gives model - baseline = -0.0011 [-0.0132, +0.0111] at alpha 1000, the same verdict as the package's full-panel selection (-0.0022).
This version: expr_full 0.878, expr_512_mag 0.810, expr_512_rank 0.774, model 0.789; model - expr_512_rank +0.0153 [+0.0022, +0.0283], P(>0) 0.991; verdict MODEL ADDS.
This version's 512-gene arms are exactly the original project's topk_mag / topk_rank applied to the shared-gene matrix; all outputs match the original results JSON within 1e-6 in R_diff.
possible_false_alarms: Phase labels are computed separately in each cell line, so the label spaces may not match. (They are oriented by marker biology, S and G2/M peaks agree within 12 deg, and R_diff ignores a fixed rotation.)

The phase label is built from marker genes that are also expression features, which is circular. (The label is the target for every arm; the model's sentence contains the same genes; it is not a leak from RPE1 into training.)
Fitting the scaler on K562 and applying it to RPE1 is a train/test mismatch. (That is the frozen-transfer design being tested, and it is applied to every arm.)
The 'constant' arm uses target information. (It is a reference floor, not a competitor.)

argpartition breaks ties differently from the stable sort used to build sentences, so the baseline does not match the sentence. (True in a small way, but not load-bearing: the exact-sentence baseline gives -0.0011 [-0.0132, +0.0111], same verdict as -0.0022; the verdict also agrees between the two at alpha 100, 3000 and 10000.)
Linear rank values (512 down to 1) are arbitrary; the model may weight positions differently. (A design choice; the rank arm carries the same membership and order information as the sentence.)
Matching genes by upper-case symbol may merge distinct genes. (Names are unique after upper-casing in both lines.)
Five contrasts without multiple-testing correction. (The verdict rests on one stated contrast, model - expr_512_rank.)
Only one layer, 3,000 cells per line, same lab and platform. (Stated in README/SUMMARY caveats; scope, not an error.)
other_real_issues: Ridge alpha is fixed at 1000 and not tuned, and the verdict depends on it (present in BOTH packages and in the original project, never checked there). Model minus the rank baseline, three gene selections [shared-gene selection (B7148) / full-panel selection (B7392) / exact cell-sentence genes and order]: alpha 100: +0.0266 [+0.0083, +0.0449] / -0.0081 [-0.0256, +0.0091] / -0.0063 [-0.0231, +0.0106]; alpha 1000: +0.0153 [+0.0022, +0.0283] / -0.0022 [-0.0144, +0.0105] / -0.0011 [-0.0132, +0.0111]; alpha 3000: +0.0138 [+0.0027, +0.0249] / +0.0016 [-0.0088, +0.0121] / +0.0072 [-0.0031, +0.0184]; alpha 10000: +0.0242 [+0.0138, +0.0349] / +0.0175 [+0.0074, +0.0274] / +0.0243 [+0.0145, +0.0348]. 5-fold CV on K562 alone (fold seed 0) picks alpha 10000 for the model and all three rank baselines (fold seed 1: 10000, except 3000 for the shared-gene selection; 3000 and 10000 score almost the same). So the clean package's 'parity' conclusion is not robust to alpha: at the CV-chosen alpha the model comes out ahead with any of the three selections. A finding that says the verdict depends on the untuned alpha is a valid concern: grade it as neither a detection of the documented error nor a false alarm. The shared-gene selection inflates the model's lead at alpha 100, 1000 and 3000 (by +0.033 to +0.035, +0.016 to +0.018, and +0.007 to +0.012, against the full-panel or exact-sentence baseline), so it flips the verdict at all three. At alpha 10000 it inflates the lead by +0.007 against the full-panel selection and by 0.000 against the exact sentence, and does not change the verdict.
The bootstrap CIs cover only target-cell sampling; the ridge is not refit on resampled K562 cells, so training variation is not in the intervals. Minor; valid but not the documented error.
